label: Edit
description: Compare knowledge-editing methods by training inputs, optimized variables, persistent updates, and preservation mechanisms. Includes explicit baselines and adjacent adaptation approaches.

rome.label: ROME
rome.title: Rank-One Model Editing
rome.summary: ROME writes **one association** into a selected MLP output matrix using a **rank-one update**. It fits the target key-value pair **exactly in the linear memory model** while minimizing changes on preservation keys.
rome.formula_explanation: The update satisfies W′k = v when C is invertible and k is nonzero. This linear constraint does not guarantee perfect end-to-end model behavior.

terms.name: Original weight
terms.description: W₀ maps MLP keys to output values.

terms.name: Rank-one correction
terms.description: k is the edit key, v the optimized target value, and C the preservation-key second moment. The outer product changes one key-value association.

terms.name: Preservation second moment
terms.description: C weights changes on background keys; the displayed inverse assumes positive definiteness.

terms.name: Single edit key
terms.description: k is averaged over subject contexts.

terms.name: Target value
terms.description: v is optimized with desired-answer likelihood and a preservation term.

steps: Select an MLP layer informed by causal tracing.
**Extract the subject key** across contexts.
**Optimize a target value** for the desired prediction.
Solve for and apply the **rank-one update**.
Evaluate edit success, paraphrase generalization, and unrelated facts.

training.edit_time_optimization: Optimize a target value with frozen model weights, then solve a rank-one insertion.
training.update_input: Subject, relation prompt, new object; sampled context prefixes.
training.supervision_target: Desired object tokens and a target internal value.
training.preservation_input: Background text for key moments; generic prompts for the target-search KL term.
training.loss_token_scope: Subject-final position for key/intervention; desired-answer NLL; separate KL prompts.
training.limitations: Exact fitting of a fixed linear key does not guarantee generated answers or dependency-aware retraction.

sources.checked_scope: Method: key extraction, value optimization, rank-one insertion

rome.paper_title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT

memit.label: MEMIT
memit.title: Mass-Editing Memory in a Transformer
memit.summary: MEMIT edits a **batch of associations** and distributes their target residuals **across selected MLP layers**. Each layer uses a **least-squares update** balancing new memories against preservation.
memit.formula_explanation: This is one layer’s update, with R = V − W₀K. C includes the scaled preservation-key second moment. MEMIT recomputes keys and allocates remaining residuals as it progresses through the selected layers.

terms.name: Original weight
terms.description: W₀ maps MLP keys to output values.

terms.name: Preservation statistic
terms.description: C is the preservation-key second moment; MEMIT absorbs its preservation scaling into C. The displayed inverse requires a nonsingular system.

terms.name: Edit keys
terms.description: K contains one key vector per requested edit.

terms.name: Residual targets
terms.description: R = V − W₀K contains the desired value changes.

terms.name: Regularized memory solve
terms.description: Balances preservation through C with fitting the batched edit keys K. Unlike an equality constraint, the fit may leave residual error.

steps: Optimize target hidden states for the requested associations.
Choose the mediating MLP layers.
At each layer, collect current keys and **allocate remaining target residuals**.
Solve the layer’s **least-squares update** and continue to the next layer.
Evaluate the batch for efficacy, generalization, and specificity.

training.edit_time_optimization: Optimize target states, then solve layerwise updates while allocating remaining residuals.
training.update_input: A batch of subject-relation-new-object edits and context prefixes.
training.supervision_target: Desired answer tokens and target hidden states.
training.limitations: The displayed relation is one layer only; layers interact through recomputed keys and residuals.

sources.checked_scope: Official method overview and linked paper

emmet.label: EMMET
emmet.title: Equality-constrained Mass Model Editing for Transformers
emmet.summary: EMMET extends ROME’s **equality-constrained memory update to batches**. It preserves old mappings while **enforcing the requested new key-value mappings** in the linear memory model.
emmet.formula_explanation: With R = V − W₀K, the ideal solution satisfies W′K = V. It assumes invertible C and KᵀC⁻¹K; dependent keys require stabilization, which can relax exact equality. Edit distribution across layers is a separate algorithmic choice.

terms.name: Original weight
terms.description: W₀ maps MLP keys to output values.

terms.name: Preservation statistic
terms.description: C is the preservation-key second moment; MEMIT absorbs its preservation scaling into C. The displayed inverse requires a nonsingular system.

terms.name: Edit keys
terms.description: K contains one key vector per requested edit.

terms.name: Residual targets
terms.description: R = V − W₀K contains the desired value changes.

terms.name: Edit-key Gram inverse
terms.description: Couples the batched equality constraints. Requires independent edit keys for the exact inverse.

terms.name: Preservation-weighted keys
terms.description: Weights the correction using C, the preservation-key second moment.

steps: Construct the batch of edit keys K and target values V.
Estimate the preservation-key second moment C.
Solve the **equality-constrained update**, using numerical stabilization where necessary.
Apply the update, optionally using a layer-distribution procedure.
Evaluate end-to-end edit success and preservation.
emmet.paper_title: A Unified Framework for Model Editing

training.edit_time_optimization: Construct targets and solve batched equality constraints.
training.update_input: Edit keys and desired values, obtained from edit examples.
training.supervision_target: Exact linear mapping of independent edit keys to target values.
training.preservation_input: Preservation keys or their second moments.
training.loss_token_scope: Target-search masks follow the chosen backbone procedure.
training.limitations: Dependent keys can make constraints incompatible; numerical stabilization can relax exact equality.

pmet.label: PMET
pmet.title: Precise Model Editing in a Transformer
pmet.summary: PMET jointly finds **attention and FFN output corrections**, \(\delta_{\mathrm{attn}}^*\) and \(\delta_{\mathrm{ffn}}^*\), for the target prediction. It then **updates only FFN weights** using the FFN correction; attention weights remain unchanged.
pmet.formula_explanation: A simplified single-key view: \(m=W_{\mathrm{FFN}}k\). The target uses **the FFN correction**, not the complete Transformer-layer correction. The full procedure distributes updates across selected layers. This is a target-fitting schematic, not the complete weight solver. PMET uses square-root residual distribution across selected layers; jointly optimized attention corrections are not written into attention weights.

terms.name: FFN output weight
terms.description: The original FFN output-projection matrix.

terms.name: Parameter update
terms.description: The correction written into FFN weights.

terms.name: FFN key
terms.description: The input activation to the output projection.

terms.name: Original FFN output
terms.description: m = W_FFN k before editing.

terms.name: Optimized FFN correction
terms.description: Obtained jointly with the attention correction; only this component supplies the FFN target.

steps: Add temporary corrections to attention and FFN outputs.
Jointly optimize \(\delta_{\mathrm{attn}}\) and \(\delta_{\mathrm{ffn}}\) for the desired prediction.
Build FFN targets from **the optimized FFN correction**.
Distribute residuals using the paper's square-root rule and solve the FFN weight updates across selected layers.
Remove temporary interventions; **keep attention weights unchanged**.

training.edit_time_optimization: Jointly optimize temporary attention/FFN output corrections, then insert only FFN targets.
training.update_input: Factual edit prompts, replacement objects, context prefixes.
training.supervision_target: Desired-answer likelihood under temporary component interventions.
training.preservation_input: Background keys and preservation terms in the original procedure.
training.loss_token_scope: Subject-associated interventions and desired-object token likelihood.
training.updated_parameters: Selected FFN output matrices; attention weights stay frozen.
training.returned_state: Edited FFN weights; temporary activation corrections are removed.
training.limitations: Removing the attention correction changes the target-search setting; matching FFN targets alone is not an end-to-end equivalence guarantee.

sources.checked_scope: PMET method and square-root residual distribution

pmet.paper_title: Precise Model Editing in a Transformer

alphaedit.label: AlphaEdit
alphaedit.title: AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Language Models
alphaedit.summary: AlphaEdit **fits new key-value associations inside a null-space-constrained update**. Original knowledge is protected by the projector; a separate penalty limits changes on **previously edited keys**, and regularization controls update size.
alphaedit.formula: \Delta_{\mathrm{AE}} = R K_1^T P ( K_pK_p^TP + K_1K_1^TP + I )^{-1},\quad W'=W+ \Delta_{\mathrm{AE}}
alphaedit.formula_explanation: Section 3.3, Eqs. (12)–(14). \(R=V_1-WK_1\). The objective combines **new-knowledge fitting**, **update regularization**, and **previous-edit preservation**. \(P=U_{\mathrm{null}}U_{\mathrm{null}}^T\) comes from SVD of \(K_0K_0^T\); exact null directions give \(\Delta_{\mathrm{AE}}K_0=0\). Small-singular-value thresholding makes that preservation approximate. The displayed identity coefficient is the unit-regularization form. A tunable positive coefficient can be written as alpha I. Preservation refers to fixed selected key mappings, not all model outputs.

terms.name: Applied update
terms.description: Δ_AE = ΔP is added to the MLP output matrix W.

terms.name: New target residual
terms.description: R = V₁ − WK₁ is what the current edit must change.

terms.name: New edit keys
terms.description: Columns of K₁ encode the current edit batch; V₁ contains target values.

terms.name: Null-space projector
terms.description: Built from preserved-key second moments K₀K₀ᵀ, protecting original key mappings.

terms.name: Previous-edit term
terms.description: K_p collects keys from previous edits; this term penalizes changes to their outputs.

terms.name: New-knowledge fitting term
terms.description: Arises from fitting the current keys K₁ to target values V₁.

terms.name: Update regularization
terms.description: The identity term comes from the squared norm of the projected update.

steps: Collect preserved keys and compute each selected layer’s second moment \(K_0K_0^T\).
Use **SVD** to construct \(P\) from zero or small singular-value directions.
Optimize new target representations and distribute remaining residuals across selected MLP layers.
Solve for the update **within the projected subspace**, accounting for previous edits and update regularization.
Apply \(W\leftarrow W+\Delta P\) and evaluate edit success and preservation.

training.edit_time_optimization: Optimize target representations and solve updates inside a preservation subspace.
training.supervision_target: Target-answer likelihood followed by layerwise value fitting.
training.preservation_input: Preserved-key second moments and historical edit keys.
training.loss_token_scope: Target-search masks follow the editing backbone.
training.limitations: Thresholded null spaces give approximate protection of sampled fixed keys, not global semantic invariance.

alphaedit.paper_title: AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Language Models

crispedit.label: CrispEdit
crispedit.title: CrispEdit: Low-Curvature Projections for Scalable Non-Destructive LLM Editing
crispedit.summary: CrispEdit projects edit gradients into **low-curvature directions of capability loss**. A **Bregman-divergence constraint** yields Gauss–Newton curvature without assuming a converged base model. K-FAC enables matrix-free projection.
crispedit.formula: Q_l^{\mathrm{proj}} = U_{\mathrm{out}} [( U_{\mathrm{out}}^T Q_l U_{\mathrm{in}} )\odot M ] U_{\mathrm{in}}^T
crispedit.formula_explanation: The capability-set Bregman objective is abbreviated. Its local quadratic term uses Gauss-Newton curvature, approximated by A\otimes S. The mask M_{ij}=\mathbf{1}[\lambda_i^{out}\lambda_j^{in}\leq\lambda_\gamma] retains low-curvature coordinates. Rotate, mask, rotate back. The displayed equation is a gradient projector, not an inverse-Hessian update. Protection is local and calibration-dependent.

terms.name: Projected gradient
terms.description: Used for the layer’s optimizer update.

terms.name: Edit gradient
terms.description: Q_l = ∇_{W_l} L_edit.

terms.name: K-FAC eigenbases
terms.description: Eigenvectors of activation and output pseudo-gradient second moments.

terms.name: Low-curvature mask
terms.description: Retains components below the spectral threshold; γ controls discarded spectral energy.

steps: Estimate **K-FAC capability curvature** and cache eigenbases and masks.
Compute edit gradients for selected layers.
**Rotate, mask high-curvature components, and rotate back** without constructing the full projector.
Apply projected-gradient optimization with the configured step rule; projecting a gradient is not automatically equivalent to projecting an Adam parameter step.
For sequential edits, accumulate curvature statistics to protect earlier edits.

training.pre_edit_training: No learned editor; precompute capability curvature.
training.edit_time_optimization: Directly optimize edit loss with curvature-restricted gradients.
training.supervision_target: Desired outputs under the edit loss.
training.preservation_input: Capability reference data for activation/pseudo-gradient second moments.
training.loss_token_scope: Explicitly configure prompt/answer masks; paper combines prompt-masked editing with projected optimization.
training.updated_parameters: Selected trainable weight matrices; scope is configuration-dependent.
training.returned_state: Edited weights and cached K-FAC statistics/bases.
training.limitations: Local curvature and capability coverage limit protection; cached geometry can become stale after large edits.

sources.checked_scope: Sections 2-3: Bregman, Gauss-Newton, K-FAC and matrix-free projection

crispedit.paper_title: CrispEdit: Low-Curvature Projections for Scalable Non-Destructive LLM Editing

fisheredit.label: FisherEdit
fisheredit.title: FisherEdit: Fisher Information Guided Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models
fisheredit.summary: FisherEdit uses **parameter-wise Fisher-weighted regularization** to protect sensitive weights while fitting new facts. It retains a historical-edit penalty and computes **row-wise closed-form updates** without null-space projection.
fisheredit.formula_explanation: Eqs. (5)–(8): \(E=V-WK_1\), \(G=K_1K_1^T+K_pK_p^T\), and \(D_i=\mathrm{diag}(F_{i,:})\). \(F\) stores empirical Fisher diagonal entries in weight-matrix shape. **High-Fisher weights receive stronger penalties**. The inverse assumes a nonsingular system; Woodbury reduces the solve when the key count is small. Empirical squared gradients on observed labels are not the exact predictive Fisher. Zero scores may require a numerical floor or damping; record the implementation choice.

terms.name: Update row
terms.description: Row i of Δ; stack rows to form the weight update.

terms.name: Target residual row
terms.description: Row i of E = V − WK₁.

terms.name: Current edit keys
terms.description: K₁ contains current keys; K_p contains historical edit keys.

terms.name: Shared key Gram matrix
terms.description: Combines current and historical key constraints.

terms.name: Regularization strength
terms.description: Scales the Fisher penalty.

terms.name: Row-specific importance
terms.description: Diagonal matrix from Fisher scores for row i.

steps: Estimate **per-example squared-gradient importance** on calibration data.
Construct current keys, target residuals, and historical keys.
Solve each update row with its Fisher-weighted penalty.
Apply the assembled update and retain keys for subsequent edits.

training.pre_edit_training: No learned editor; estimate importance before editing.
training.edit_time_optimization: Optimize value targets, then solve each update row with Fisher-weighted penalties.
training.supervision_target: Target values and desired answer tokens.
training.preservation_input: Labeled calibration examples for per-example squared gradients; historical keys.
training.loss_token_scope: Calibration CE uses the stated label mask; record target-search token scope separately.
training.returned_state: Edited weights, empirical Fisher scores, historical-key statistics.
training.limitations: Diagonal empirical importance is a proxy; row systems require nonsingularity or documented stabilization.

sources.checked_scope: Sections 4.1-4.4: objective, row solver and empirical Fisher

fisheredit.paper_title: FisherEdit: Fisher Information Guided Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models

knowledgeeditor.label: KE
knowledgeeditor.title: Editing Factual Knowledge in Language Models
knowledgeeditor.summary: Train a hypernetwork to predict targeted weight changes under preservation constraints.
knowledgeeditor.formula_explanation: Schematic interface; request encodings and gradient conditioning follow the implementation.

terms.name: Learned editor
terms.description: phi parameterizes the update generator.

steps: Train on edit requests and locality examples.
Encode a new request and gradient features.
Predict and apply the parameter update.

mend.summary: Train small networks to transform activation and gradient factors into useful parameter updates.
mend.formula_explanation: Normalized schematic: transformed input factors u and output-gradient factors g form an update; scaling and aggregation follow the implementation.

malmen.formula_explanation: Normalized aggregation schematic; U contains input activations and V_phi contains learned target changes.

terms.name: Least-squares aggregation
terms.description: Couples multiple learned edit signals through shared keys.

Solve and apply the aggregated update.

schema_notes.compatibility: Existing method IDs and display fields are retained. New fields are additive; renderers must opt in to group and keyword filters.
schema_notes.keywords: Arrays contain stable IDs from keyword_catalog. Display labels and facets are defined centrally.
schema_notes.classification: Each method has one navigation group. Keywords and filters support overlapping mechanisms.
schema_notes.formula_status: normalized_core = core relation in unified notation; schematic = conceptual summary; baseline = configurable baseline, not a unique paper algorithm.
schema_notes.training: pre_edit_training and edit_time_optimization describe different stages. Optimizing an activation correction does not itself change base weights.
schema_notes.sources: Primary-source content review; no claim of implementation reproduction. Generic baseline recipes are labeled explicitly.
schema_notes.evaluation: Use generated answers, generalization, locality, and capability tests; a linear key-value equality is not an end-to-end guarantee.
schema_notes.formula_tokens: Render tokens as math fragments; formula uses whitespace between fragments to avoid accidental TeX control-word concatenation.
schema_notes.base_weight_filter: Refers to original base tensors during the default edit procedure; LoRA keeps them frozen until an optional explicit merge. Side memories and activation values are separate state.

filters.label: Changes original base weights at edit time

review_notes: Corrected ROME term definitions that previously mixed single-key notation with MEMIT batch notation.
Separated temporary activation optimization from persistent weight changes, especially for PMET.
Added PMET square-root residual allocation and the distinction between target-search and deployment states.
Clarified that AlphaEdit uses a unit regularization coefficient in the displayed formula and only preserves fixed selected key mappings under the exact projector assumptions.
Clarified that CrispEdit uses a K-FAC gradient projector, not inverse-Hessian preconditioning; generic Adam steps need separate treatment.
Distinguished empirical diagonal Fisher from predictive Fisher and documented row-solver numerical assumptions.
Added 12 representative baselines, learned editors, memory methods and adjacent adaptation methods; this is not an exhaustive editing survey.
Added a controlled keyword catalog, six method groups, structured training fields and explicit formula-status labels.
